solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vehicle taking rough road north stopping prematurely

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading the letters upwards, from bottom to top
the word ends before its final letter, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a track is a rough unmade road

explanation.surface: A vehicle on a bumpy road heading north grinds to a halt too early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping prematurely' cuts TRACK to TRAC; 'north' turns it upwards in this down clue to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart is a simple wheeled vehicle, often drawn by a horse.

clue.text: Fellow in charge penning article that's mad

definitions.note: used as an adjective; the answer can be an adjective meaning wildly insane

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man in charge writes something with an article that is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's mad' reads as a comment on the fellow, but 'mad' alone is the definition, used in the adjective sense the answer also has.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes someone frenzied or insane, a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: Element extracted from quartz in chemistry

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the words that follow, quartz in chemistry

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson on getting an element out of quartz.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, number 30 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Man who has transgressed looking heavenward

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up to heaven means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: to transgress is to sin, so one who has transgressed has sinned

explanation.surface: A sinner looks up to heaven in repentance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking heavenward' reverses SINNED in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis is a common male first name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Chemical substance obtainable from isocline

indicators.note: the letters of the next word can be rearranged to produce the answer

explanation.surface: A chemical that can be extracted from a geological feature called an isocline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtainable from' signals rearranging all eight letters of ISOCLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicones are synthetic polymers used in sealants and lubricants, a type of chemical compound.

clue.text: Daringly innovative parent with home in a mess

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are jumbled up as if left in a mess

explanation.surface: A bold parent whose house is untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' signals scrambling PARENT and HOME together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus defied the gods to give humans fire, so Promethean means boldly creative or original.

clue.text: The old woman had briefly organised one Indian lady

parts.note: the old woman is a familiar term for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of had goes

parts.note: to run something is to organise it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mother briefly ran things for a single Indian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharani is the wife of a maharaja or a female Indian ruler.

clue.text: Firm's first male worker

parts.note: in the Bible Adam was the first man
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A company's first male employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective meaning resolute; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding and resolute, a synonym of firm in attitude.

clue.text: One deciding to leave country before catching plane

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a MiG is a Russian military plane

explanation.surface: Someone emigrating who must make a flight before it departs.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is a person who has left their own country, often for political reasons.

clue.text: Barbarian got down with army heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to get down
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force

explanation.surface: A barbarian dismounts and leads his army westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' reverses ALITTA as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun was the fifth-century ruler famed as the archetypal barbarian.

clue.text: Establishes companies, initiated by trick

indicators.note: initiated by means started by, so the trick comes first

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
firms are companies

explanation.surface: Companies set up through a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to establish its truth or make it settled.

clue.text: Magazine's left something for fans to enjoy looking at

definitions.text: something for fans to enjoy looking at

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly political magazine, with the possessive s kept
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A magazine has abandoned something its readers enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Magazine's supplies the final S of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator sport is one people watch for enjoyment, so fans enjoy viewing it.

clue.text: Drink on select island — bar entrance with this maybe?

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
to cull is to select, as from a flock

explanation.surface: Wine served on a chosen island, and a question about barring a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a verb here: a castle gate's grille bars the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is a heavy grating lowered to block a castle gateway.

clue.text: College learner follows Conservatives, avoiding extremes

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the learner goes at the end
the first and last letters of the word are left off

parts.note: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student at college trails behind Conservatives while shunning radical views.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Balance end of object on edge

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word object

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Advice on balancing an item by placing its end on a ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim is the balance of a boat or aircraft, the way it sits in the water or air.

clue.text: Letters presenting a unified image?

parts.note: initials woven together into a single design; read cryptically, one-written picture, from Greek mono and gramma

explanation.definitionFit: A monogram is a design of interwoven initials forming one emblem.

clue.text: The Yorkshire bumpkin is stupid

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is shortened to t'
a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire yokel is called dim.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire dialect 'the' is cut to t'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal British for dull-witted or slow, a synonym of dim.

clue.text: Dough may be required by the sound of it

indicators.note: the words are said aloud and heard as another word with different spelling

parts.note: required means needed

explanation.surface: Money may be necessary, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like slang for money; it is bread dough, which is worked by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dough is pressed and worked by hand, which is what being kneaded means.

clue.text: A woman's right at all times

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in the Bible, stands for a woman; the possessive gives no letter

explanation.surface: A woman is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, as in 'ever faithful'.

clue.text: This being put on should ensure more than just a warm reception

definitions.text: This being put on should ensure more than just a warm reception

parts.words: This being put on should ensure more than just a warm reception
parts.note: a warm reception sounds like a friendly welcome, but here it is a heated reception room and the rest of the house too

explanation.definitionFit: A heating system run from one boiler warms every room of a house, not just the hall.

clue.text: This person blocking the way was a nomad

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a road is a way
this person means the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Someone standing in the path was a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place, so being one means having roamed.

clue.text: Display of irritation about a restaurant's opening menu

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: a tiff is a minor bad-tempered quarrel

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of restaurant's

explanation.surface: Someone gets annoyed about a restaurant's first menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of charges or prices, such as a hotel or restaurant price list.

clue.text: Gross female prisoner having angry words

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag
a rant is a loud angry speech

explanation.surface: A woman inmate shouting furiously is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaring and shocking, as in a gross or flagrant breach.

clue.text: Old books turned up, your writer providing one volume

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible
your writer is the setter, me

explanation.surface: Old books surface, the author offering a single volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, especially a large heavy one.

clue.text: Descend in plunge, concealing hesitation

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a dive is a plunge
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone goes down in a dive while hiding their nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive from something is to descend or originate from it.

clue.text: See contest won with cricket side eliminated

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

indicators.note: eliminated means removed, so those letters come out of the word won

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batter's legs

explanation.surface: A contest won once a cricket team has been knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... eliminated' takes ON from WON to leave W; the on side in cricket is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is to see or look at.

clue.text: Very small star, about four, seen to be lively

parts.note: V is the small, abbreviated form of very
IV is four in Roman numerals
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A tiny star of about four seems energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'seen to be' are link words; V is the short form of very, as in musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivace is the musical direction meaning to play in a lively, brisk manner.

clue.text: Government department, if that is dead, must be changed

parts.note: MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a UK government department
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ministry, if it is defunct, must be reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Modified means altered or adjusted, a synonym of changed.
